correctness.rationale: For i≠j the entry is h(a_ij−hΔ_ij/2); missing edges and edges with Δ_ij≤0 cannot constrain h≥0. The diagonal is at least [1+(1−hλ_i)^2]/2, and row sums are one. In a row of maximal exit rate M>0 the diagonal exceeds one for h>2/M, so some constraining edge exists. Every constraining entry stays negative after its first positive zero, which proves the entire interval, not just a first crossing. Dividing Δ_ij by a_ij gives a denominator at most 2M, with equality exactly when both exits are maximal and the two-step alternative has zero weight. The star has threshold 2/(m+1); even exact equality in the upper universal bound is possible for a single one-way edge to an absorbing vertex. Q=0 is handled separately; the regular common-neighbor formula is for d>0.
residual_risks: Finite rational assertion groups are supporting diagnostics, not needed for the proof for real rates. This result does not certify intermediate-stage positivity.
